title: Artemis I lunar flyby radiation measurements

measurement_definition.warning: Absorbed dose rate is not dose equivalent rate. Do not infer dose equivalent from these values.

comparison_method: Compare the mean absorbed dose rate from the two hours before closest approach, the two-hour interval centred on closest approach, and the two hours after closest approach. The percentage compares the near-window mean with the average of the before and after means.

scientific_interpretation.published_finding: The Nature Artemis I study reports that the Moon blocks part of the incoming galactic cosmic-ray sky during close flybys, reducing GCR dose rates by approximately one-third.
scientific_interpretation.dataset_caution: The phase averages in this dataset are a separate descriptive calculation. They do not independently establish the cause of observed changes or reproduce the paper's full analysis.
scientific_interpretation.game_use: Suitable for a learning scenario about the Moon blocking some incoming space radiation. Any game effect must be identified as a simulation, not a measured protection percentage.

quality_notes: All four instruments are retained separately.
HERA sampling is one minute; EAD and M42 sampling is five minutes.
The comparison windows are descriptive, not a controlled experiment.
No missing measurement has been replaced with zero.
Original raw files were not modified.

research_reference.title: Space radiation measurements during the Artemis I lunar mission
